entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J.

The instant appeal is preferred by the appellant Jaspal challenging his conviction and sentence under Sections 363, 376, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, recorded on 17.07.2025/18.07.2025 in Special Sessions Trial No. 137 of 2016,
State of Uttarakhand v. Jaspal, by the court of Special Judge (POCSO)/Additional District Judge,
Dehradun.
2.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: This is an admitted appeal.
3. The appellant seeks bail during pendency of the appeal.

4. Heard learned counsel for the parties on the bail application and perused the record.
5.
According to the FIR, on 01.09.2018, the victim revealed that the applicant used to molest her and one day raped her in a room.
The victim could not reveal the incident to anyone immediately after the incident.
But, subsequently she revealed it to her father, who lodged the FIR.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the conviction is based on the sole testimony of the victim, which is not reliable; her statement does not find corroboration either from medical or any other material; she had not gone to show the place of incident to the Investigating Officer, but the Investigating Officer has prepared a site plan; it also doubts the prosecution case.

He also Unknown vs State Of Uttarakhand on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25338153/
1 submits that the applicant was called in the house of the informant on 01.09.2018 and thereafter he was handed over to the police, and on 02.09.2018, the FIR has been lodged.
7.

entities.text: Unknown vs State Of Uttarakhand on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is a bail, post conviction.
The appellant does not have the benefit of presumption of innocence.
He is a convict.
Whatever observation is made in this order, confines to this bail order only.
8. According to the victim, she was in talking terms with the appellant on WhatsApp, as she had accepted his friend request.
On 23.08.2018, the appellant called her and raped her in his house.
Again, he called the victim on Saturday, 25.08.2018, and told the victim that he will be visiting her house.
Thereafter, the victim revealed the incident to her parents and the appellant was apprehended and sent to the police.
In her statement, she states that after the incident of 23.08.2018, on 25.08.2018, the appellant telephoned her and asked that he would visit her house, to which the victim declined.

Thereafter, she revealed the incident on 01.09.2018 and on 02.09.2018,
the report was lodged.

9. According to the Investigating Officer, he prepared the site plan at the instance of the victim,
whereas the victim has categorically stated that she never visited the place of incident subsequent to the incident.
Admittedly, there is no injury.
10. Having considered this and other attending factors, this Court is of the view that it is a case in which the execution of the sentence should be suspended and the appellant be enlarged on bail.
11. The bail application is allowed.
12. The execution of sentence appealed against is suspended during the pendency of the appeal.

13. Let the appellant Jaspal be released on bail, during the pendency of the appeal, on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the court concerned.
14.
List the criminal appeal for final hearing in due course.

(Ravindra Maithani, J) 07.11.2025 Avneet/
